claims.text: In situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction can elucidate oxidation mechanisms in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
In situ HTXRD can elucidate elemental redistribution from nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
HTXRD provides real-time phase identification and structural-evolution tracking under controlled oxidation conditions.
Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 has a dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure.
The evaluated Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy is produced by additive manufacturing.
The additively manufactured alloy contains well-dispersed nanoprecipitates.
The alloy can be examined by simultaneous in situ XRD while it is exposed to a controlled high-temperature oxidation environment.
A temperature range of approximately 700–1100 °C in air or controlled oxygen partial pressure is suitable for initiating oxidation in this alloy.
Nanoprecipitates may act as preferential oxidation sites.
Nanoprecipitates may influence whether protective or non-protective oxide layers form.
High-temperature environmental exposure can induce phase transformations in an HEA.
Oxidation induces elemental redistribution from nanoprecipitates in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
HTXRD can capture transient oxide phases during oxidation.
XRD lattice-parameter shifts can be used to infer oxidation mechanisms and elemental migration.
In situ XRD will reveal the emergence and evolution of oxide phases and associated lattice-parameter shifts.
The XRD changes can be correlated with redistribution of specific alloying elements from nanoprecipitates.
The oxidation behavior of the additively manufactured alloy will differ from that of conventionally processed counterparts.
Cast or wrought variants of the alloy lack the dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure used as the structural mediator.
Laboratory-scale time-resolved oxidation measurements may not capture long-term behavior in industrial applications.
Ex situ electron microscopy and EDS mapping can validate phase and elemental-redistribution interpretations from HTXRD.
